delivery.outcome: Every opted-in Wellmanifest domain standard has one deterministic C/Q authority with mandatory event and error catalogs
nonGoals: No forced CQRS structure for ordinary application repositories
No runtime event bus, command dispatcher or generated application code
No migration of existing standards outside their own tickets
No protobuf or JSON Schema promotion to semantic source of truth

architecture.decision: Use an optional closed manifest mode whose CQRS variant fixes operations/index.json as the sole command/query authority and validates referenced event and error catalogs
interfaceChanges: Governance manifests may declare a closed domainContracts mode
Opted-in standards must publish operations, events and error registries
The governance checker validates C/Q/Event/Error cross-references
dataChanges: The default manifest reserves integration-owned operations, events, error, models and proto namespaces
architecture.rollback: Revert the optional manifest property, checker, default ownership paths and managed prose; existing manifests remain valid throughout

validation.evidence: Schema and direct policy assertions accept only the closed none/cqrs forms
Adversarial fixtures reject missing catalogs, duplicate C/Q authority and broken graph references

commands: for test in tests/*.test.sh; do bash "$test"; done
validation.evidence: Full Linux contract covers a positive CQRS fixture and existing backward-compatible fixtures
